clauses.reason: The operative sentence says: "do hereby approve said Amendment and modify my previous approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry by Executive Order dated December 9, 1933, my approval of the said Code as amended by Executive Order dated April 20, 1934, and my approval of said Code as amended by Executive Order dated June 29, 1934, to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended". It is a section 3 approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry as amended, so its operative effect was the code's legal force. Under section 3(b) of the Act the approved code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade or industry, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations, and under 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor; that force was the whole operative effect of an approval. The order states no period, condition, 'until' date, stay or provisional approval of its own, and no held record cancels, suspends, modifies under section 10(b) or supersedes the code before June 14, 1935 (see earlier_end_check). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 (Pub. Res. No. 26, 74th Cong., 49 Stat. 375, approved June 14, 1935) provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The resolution states no effective date other than its approval on June 14, 1935. Repeal of the power to approve codes and of the provisions enforcing them removed the legal force that the approval gave the code, so this clause ended on June 14, 1935; effective date confirmed. June 16, 1935, Title I's original two-year expiry, is not an end date: section 1 of the resolution replaced it with April 1, 1936. A. L. A. Schechter Poultry Corp. v. United States, decided May 27, 1935, held the section 3 delegation unconstitutional; it is recorded as a validity characterization (an approval made under an unconstitutional delegation was void from issuance under the doctrine then prevailing), not as an end date, because the decision cancelled no approving order and no held record shows this code cancelled or suspended on May 27, 1935.

inventory_overrides.reason: The machine inventory lists findings 1 to 5 as five clauses. Findings 1 to 4 and the findings recital in clause 5 are the President's statutory findings (application, notice, hearings, compliance with section 3(a), tendency to effectuate the policy of the Act); they command nothing. The only operative command is the second 'Now, Therefore' sentence, "do hereby approve said Amendment and modify my previous approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry" through "as hereby amended", which this single corrected span covers.

savings.reason: Acts done under the approved code before June 14, 1935, and any liability for violating it before that date, are accrued effects. The general savings statute of the time (not a held source) preserved liabilities already incurred under a repealed statute; that preservation does not keep the approval operative. Section 5 of the Act exempted from the antitrust laws "any code, agreement, or license approved, prescribed, or issued and in effect under this title" and complying action while Title I was in effect and for sixty days after; whatever exemption survives for action taken before the repeal is an accrued effect. The proviso in section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 says the exemption "shall extend only to agreements and action thereunder" of two kinds (section 7(a) requirements, and prohibiting practices already unlawful); it names agreements, not codes, and states no time limit, so the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action taken under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source continues this approval after June 14, 1935 and no held source shows a prosecution continued after that date.
